name: Common Prepositions
description: Practice common prepositions for time, place, movement, method, tools, and duration in clear everyday contexts.

cards.front: The meeting begins at the exact clock time 8:30. Complete: The meeting starts ___ 8:30.
cards.answer: The meeting starts at 8:30.
cards.explanation: Use “at” with an exact clock time.
cards.example: The film ends at 9:45.
options: The meeting starts at 8:30.
The meeting starts on 8:30.
The meeting starts in 8:30.

cards.front: The appointment is scheduled for Tuesday. Complete: My appointment is ___ Tuesday.
cards.answer: My appointment is on Tuesday.
cards.explanation: Use “on” with a day of the week.
cards.example: We have a team lunch on Friday.
options: My appointment is on Tuesday.
My appointment is at Tuesday.
My appointment is in Tuesday.

cards.front: The course begins during the month of July. Complete: The course begins ___ July.
cards.answer: The course begins in July.
cards.explanation: Use “in” with a month.
cards.example: The new semester starts in September.
options: The course begins in July.
The course begins on July.
The course begins at July.

cards.front: The keys are resting on the top surface of the desk. Complete: The keys are ___ the desk.
cards.answer: The keys are on the desk.
cards.explanation: Use “on” when something touches a surface.
cards.example: Your notebook is on the kitchen table.
options: The keys are on the desk.
The keys are in the desk.
The keys are under the desk.

cards.front: The receipt is inside a closed drawer. Complete: The receipt is ___ the drawer.
cards.answer: The receipt is in the drawer.
cards.explanation: Use “in” when something is inside an enclosed space.
cards.example: There is some fruit in the bowl.
options: The receipt is in the drawer.
The receipt is on the drawer.
The receipt is beside the drawer.

cards.front: Kai is waiting where everyone agreed to meet: the building’s entrance. Complete: Kai is waiting ___ the entrance.
cards.answer: Kai is waiting at the entrance.
cards.explanation: Use “at” for a specific point or meeting place.
cards.example: I will meet you at the front desk.
options: Kai is waiting at the entrance.
Kai is waiting on the entrance.

cards.front: The bakery is directly beside the pharmacy. Complete: The bakery is ___ the pharmacy.
cards.answer: The bakery is next to the pharmacy.
cards.explanation: “Next to” means directly beside something or someone.
cards.example: A small park is next to the library.
options: The bakery is next to the pharmacy.
The bakery is across from the pharmacy.
The bakery is behind the pharmacy.

cards.front: The café has the bank on one side and the post office on the other. Complete: The café is ___ the bank and the post office.
cards.answer: The café is between the bank and the post office.
cards.explanation: Use “between” for something in the middle of two distinct people, places, or things.
cards.example: The lamp stands between the two chairs.
options: The café is between the bank and the post office.
The café is among the bank and the post office.

cards.front: The bag is on the floor below the chair. Complete: The bag is ___ the chair.
cards.answer: The bag is under the chair.
cards.explanation: Use “under” when something is lower than another object and directly below it.
cards.example: The cat is sleeping under the table.
options: The bag is under the chair.
The bag is above the chair.

cards.front: A picture hangs higher than the sofa without touching it. Complete: The picture is ___ the sofa.
cards.answer: The picture is above the sofa.
cards.explanation: Use “above” when something is at a higher position than something else.
cards.example: A clock hangs above the doorway.
options: The picture is above the sofa.
The picture is below the sofa.

cards.front: The library is our destination. Complete: We are walking ___ the library.
cards.answer: We are walking to the library.
cards.explanation: Use “to” for movement toward a destination.
cards.example: Emi cycled to the market after work.
options: We are walking to the library.
We are walking from the library.
We are walking at the library.

cards.front: The airport is the starting point of this bus route. Complete: This bus comes ___ the airport.
cards.answer: This bus comes from the airport.
cards.explanation: Use “from” to identify the origin or starting point of movement.
cards.example: The package came from a warehouse nearby.
options: This bus comes from the airport.
This bus comes to the airport.

cards.front: The child moved from the hallway to the inside of the room. Complete: The child walked ___ the room.
cards.answer: The child walked into the room.
cards.explanation: Use “into” for movement from outside to inside a place.
cards.example: A bird flew into the open garage.
options: The child walked into the room.
The child walked out of the room.

cards.front: The workers moved from inside the building to the street. Complete: The workers came ___ the building.
cards.answer: The workers came out of the building.
cards.explanation: Use “out of” for movement from inside a place to outside it.
cards.example: Steam came out of the kettle.
options: The workers came out of the building.
The workers came into the building.
The workers came under the building.

cards.front: They walked from one side of the street to the other. Complete: They walked ___ the street at the crossing.
cards.answer: They walked across the street at the crossing.
cards.explanation: Use “across” for movement from one side of a surface or area to the other.
cards.example: We ran across the field before the rain started.
options: They walked across the street at the crossing.
They walked along the street at the crossing.

cards.front: The train entered one end of the tunnel and exited the other. Complete: The train went ___ the tunnel.
cards.answer: The train went through the tunnel.
cards.explanation: Use “through” for movement within an enclosed space from one side to another.
cards.example: Sunlight came through the window.
options: The train went through the tunnel.
The train went across the tunnel.
The train went beside the tunnel.

cards.front: A train was the method of transport for our trip. Complete: We traveled ___ train.
cards.answer: We traveled by train.
cards.explanation: Use “by” before a transport method when no article or possessive comes before the vehicle.
cards.example: The group traveled by bus.
options: We traveled by train.
We traveled on train.
We traveled with train.

cards.front: No vehicle was used; I walked home. Complete: I went home ___ foot.
cards.answer: I went home on foot.
cards.explanation: “On foot” is the fixed expression for traveling by walking.
cards.example: The station is close enough to reach on foot.
options: I went home on foot.
I went home by foot.
I went home at foot.

cards.front: Scissors were the tool used to open the package. Complete: I opened the package ___ scissors.
cards.answer: I opened the package with scissors.
cards.explanation: Use “with” to name the tool used to perform an action.
cards.example: She stirred the soup with a wooden spoon.
options: I opened the package with scissors.
I opened the package by scissors.
I opened the package from scissors.

cards.front: The study session lasted two hours. Complete: We studied ___ two hours.
cards.answer: We studied for two hours.
cards.explanation: Use “for” to state the duration of an action or situation.
cards.example: We waited for twenty minutes.
options: We studied for two hours.
We studied at two hours.
We studied from two hours.
